name: Missouri
basePeriod: The first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before your claim. Missouri has no alternate base period.
notModeled: The second wage test is 1.5 times the taxable wage base, $9,000 for 2026; a claim measured against 2025's $9,500 would need $14,250.

citation.sourceNote: RSMo 288.038: "four percent" of "the average of the two highest quarters of the worker's base period", at most "three hundred twenty dollars", rounded down. 288.030: "one thousand five hundred dollars or more in at least one calendar quarter" and a total of 1.5 times it, or wages in two quarters totaling "one and one-half times the maximum taxable wage base" ($9,000 for 2026, DES). 288.060.4, the operative 2011 text: the total "shall not exceed twenty times his or her weekly benefit amount, or thirty-three and one-third percent of his or her wage credits." The 2015 HB 150 version on the revisor's site, which indexed weeks to unemployment, was voided in Pestka v. State (2016); DES: "Twenty weeks of benefits is the maximum". No dependent allowance; one waiting week, paid at the end of the claim. Read 2026-10-19.
